messages:
oliver: Quick note from the new-model canary (sparrow-mini-ptq4). We see structured tool-calls occasionally missing the "actions" field only when streaming is enabled. Minimal raw fragments below.

mei: Paste the raw fragments pls.

oliver: Two consecutive chunks (order preserved):

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"{\"req\":\"q7\",\"resp\":{\"status\":\"ok\",\"actions\":[{\"cmd\":\"write\",\"params\":{\"path\":\"/tmp/log\",\""}
```

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"\"payload\":\"done\"}}]}},\n"}
```

oliver: Reassembly sometimes yields actions:null or parser throws invalid UTF-8. Quantized model (PTQ-4) fails ~3.5% vs fp16 ~0.4% on same prompts.

diego: "invalid UTF-8" is interesting — could be tokenizer emitting splits that break multi-byte UTF8 sequences. That can cause the parser to error before we can reassemble.

mei: Short-term: try varint-length prefix framing at the runtime ingress (smaller overhead vs sentinel wrappers) + a lightweight CRC16. That way reassembler reads full record even across arbitrary chunk cuts.

frank: Also propose "utf8-safe-chunking" in the runtime: ensure chunk boundaries do not split UTF-8 codepoints by peeking a few bytes ahead and buffering until a codepoint boundary. Cheap to check and should drastically reduce parse errors caused by mid-codepoint cuts.

oliver: Ran a small A/B: N=1000 adversarial splits (simulate cuts anywhere). Results: fp16 parse-fail 0.5%, ptq4 3.4%. With varint-len+CRC16: ptq4 -> 0.2%. With utf8-safe-chunking only: ptq4 -> 0.8% but <10ms p95 increase. Combined both: ptq4 -> 0.05%.

runtime-bot: feature 7123456789: toggles applied: `varint_len_pref=true`, `crc16_check=true`, `utf8_safe_chunking=true` on 5% canary at 16:22 UTC. Monitoring active.

diego: Nice. Next steps: run a 5k sweep across fp16/PTQ4/hybrid, capture parse-fail, retry-rate, p50/p95 latency, and extra tokens. Also add a tiny unit test that fuzzes mid-byte splits.

mei: I'll own the sweep and upload results here. Also will open an RFC for adding a tokenizer-level reserved token (single-byte sentinel) during future model finetune so models can explicitly mark JSON boundaries without extra framing overhead.

oliver: Thanks team — will follow up with logs and metrics in this thread. :rocket:
